description:
Goal

A callable-mapper overload preserves its mapper input from producer-owned callable use through activation, runtime demand, transport, and native lowering. Inputs are omitted only when settled semantic demand proves they are unused.

Current proof

Enum.with_index(["a", "b"], fn(x, _index) -> x <> "!" end) returns ["a!", "b!"] in the backend interpreter. JIT and AOT fail before execution because native clause dispatch requires omitted semantic input 1 for the with_index activation. The callable exists and is selected; its mapper input was incorrectly classified as non-runtime before native lowering.

Strategy

Trace BackendExecutable input 1 backward through transport and RuntimeDemand to the first authoritative fact that omitted it. Refine that producer/use conclusion there. Do not add a native fallback, decode an ActivationKey, inspect payloads downstream, or force all overload inputs live. Preserve omission for genuinely unused inputs.

Acceptance

The isolated callback repro and the string, integer, and tuple mapper variants in enum_map_family pass interp, run, and build with oracle output. A focused production-path signal pins the mapper input as present at the first boundary that formerly dropped it. No reconstruction or fallback is introduced; library tests and strict clippy pass.
title: Preserve Enum.with_index callable mapper input through native lowering
